Abstract.AbstractText: The chemical characteristic of a well-known folk medicine Ganoderma lucidum has been investigated by a series of chromatographic technologies, which displayed the presences of 45 lanostane type triterpenoids, including two new nor-lanostane triterpenoids (40, 41). Their structures were identified on the basis of spectroscopic data analysis (UV, IR, HRESIMS, 1D, and 2D NMR). Notably, some triterpenoids displayed moderate inhibitory effects against AChE (acetylcholinesterase) by an in vitro screened experiment. Triterpenoid 2 displayed the potent inhibitory effect with IC50 10.8 and Ki 14.95 μM (inhibition kinetic). The preliminary SAR has been discussed by the docking analyses between ganoderic acids (1, 2) and AChE.
